mainTopic: The limits of מעילה after a מצוה and the exclusions for blood; the rule that the יום הכיפורים service must follow its order
overview: The amud opens by finishing the question of why we cannot learn from תרומת הדשן that מעילה applies to every holy item after its מצוה is done. The answer is that two verses sharing the same unusual law teach nothing to other cases (שני כתובין הבאין כאחד אין מלמדין). For the רבנן the second case is the בגדי כהונה, and for רבי דוסא it is עגלה ערופה. For the view that such pairs do teach, the limiting words ״ושמו״ and ״הערופה״ block a general rule. The גמרא then explains that the three verses about blood each remove blood from a different law: נותר, מעילה, and טומאה. No verse is needed for פיגול, because blood is itself the מתיר. A new משנה then rules that the יום הכיפורים service must be done in order, and it explains what happens if the blood spills partway through the sprinklings. In the גמרא, רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה disagree about which parts of the service the order rule covers. רבי יוחנן says both learn their views from one פסוק, and their readings are explained on the next amud.

steps.title: תרומת הדשן and בגדי כהונה are two verses that come as one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that we cannot learn a general rule from תרומת הדשן. The same unusual law also appears with the בגדי כהונה, and two verses that teach the same unusual law do not teach other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because תרומת הדשן and the בגדי כהונה are two verses that come as one, and any two verses that come as one do not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the earlier question of why we don't learn from תרומת הדשן that every holy item stays under מעילה after its מצוה. The answer is that the Torah repeated this rule in two places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, one example in the Torah can serve as a model for other cases. But when the Torah states the same unusual rule twice, it shows that the rule is limited to those cases. If it applied everywhere, one verse would have been enough. So תרומת הדשן together with the בגדי כהונה are treated as exceptions, not models.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily removal of a scoop of ashes from the מזבח, which is placed beside it
Priestly garments; here, the four white garments of the כהן גדול on יום כיפור
Two verses that come as one, meaning two places in the Torah that share the same unusual law
They do not teach; we may not learn other cases from them

steps.confusionAlert: It seems backwards that two sources should teach less than one source. The logic is that if the rule were general, the Torah would not have needed to repeat it. The repetition shows the rule is limited to those two cases.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic tool of Torah interpretation used all across ש״ס. It is also the reason the general rule stays: once a מצוה is done, its object is usually no longer under מעילה.

phrases.english: Because the removal of the ashes is
phrases.notes: מעילה applies to the ashes even after the מצוה, learned from ״ושמו אצל המזבח״

phrases.english: and the priestly garments
phrases.notes: The white garments of יום כיפור, learned from ״והניחם שם״

phrases.english: two verses that come as one,
and any two verses that come as one
do not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵי תְּרוּמַת הַדֶּשֶׁן וּבִגְדֵי כְהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question on the previous amud: why not learn from תרומת הדשן that מעילה applies after every completed מצוה?
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the source by using an interpretive rule (שני כתובין הבאין כאחד)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תרומת הדשן could be a model showing that all holy items stay under מעילה after their מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the בגדי כהונה share the same unusual law, the two together are exceptions and teach nothing to other cases.

steps.title: רבי דוסא removes the בגדי כהונה as a second case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the answer works for the רבנן, who hold the garments must be buried. But according to רבי דוסא, the garments may be reused by an ordinary כהן, so there is no second case.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the רבנן, who say: "and he shall leave them there" teaches that they need burial. But for רבי דוסא, who said the priestly garments are fit for an ordinary כהן, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 1. It shows that, according to רבי דוסא, the second case disappears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 1 needs two cases. The garments count as a second case only if they stay holy and must be hidden away, which is what the רבנן learn from ״והניחם שם״. רבי דוסא holds an ordinary כהן may wear them, so they are not under מעילה. That leaves תרומת הדשן alone, and one case alone should be able to teach a general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (opening of a challenge: it fits one view but not another)
"And he shall leave them there" (ויקרא טז:כג), said about the white garments
They need burial or hiding away; they cannot be used again
An ordinary כהן, not the כהן גדול
What is there to say? (the answer seems not to work)

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase הניחא לרבנן is not the conclusion. It only sets up the real difficulty, which comes with אלא לרבי דוסא.

phrases.english: This works well according to the Rabbis, who say:
"and he shall leave them there"
teaches that they require burial.
But according to Rabbi Dosa, who said:
the priestly garments are fit
for an ordinary priest,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 1 by showing it depends on one side of a מחלוקת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 1 that the בגדי כהונה are the second of the two verses
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי דוסא, the garments do not need burial and are not under מעילה. That leaves only one case (תרומת הדשן), and one case should be able to teach a general rule.

steps.title: Ashes and the עגלה ערופה are the two verses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that, for רבי דוסא, the second case is עגלה ערופה, which stays forbidden for benefit after its מצוה. So there are still two verses that come as one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה are two verses that come as one, and any two verses that come as one do not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by replacing the priestly garments with a different second case: the עגלה ערופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עגלה ערופה stays forbidden for benefit even after its מצוה is done, just like the ashes. So even רבי דוסא has two cases sharing this unusual law, and the rule of שני כתובין הבאין כאחד still blocks learning to other cases. The next step asks whether this works for the view that such pairs do teach.

keyTerms.meaning: The calf whose neck is broken when a murdered body is found and the killer is unknown; it stays forbidden for benefit afterward

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that holiness and מעילה stay after a מצוה is done is limited to special cases. Both the רבנן and רבי דוסא agree it does not spread to other cases. For the רבנן, the pair is ashes and garments. For רבי דוסא, the pair is ashes and עגלה ערופה.
steps.confusionAlert: עגלה ערופה is about a forbidden-benefit law (איסור הנאה), not literally the מעילה of הקדש. The shared point is that the item stays forbidden even after its מצוה is complete.

phrases.english: Because the removal of the ashes
and the heifer whose neck is broken
phrases.notes: Forbidden for benefit even after its מצוה is complete

phrases.english: are two verses that come as one,
and any two verses that come as one
do not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵי תְּרוּמַת הַדֶּשֶׁן וְעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 2 by finding a different second case that works even for רבי דוסא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Swaps in a replacement source (another parallel case)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the garments, תרומת הדשן stands alone according to רבי דוסא and could teach a general rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: עגלה ערופה is the second case, so the two-verses rule still applies and nothing is learned to other cases.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Even according to רבי דוסא, there are still two cases (תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה), so the rule of שני כתובין הבאין כאחד אין מלמדין blocks a general rule. Step 4 challenges this for the opposing view, and Step 5 completes the answer.

steps.title: The answer only works for one opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the 'two verses that come as one' answer. It works for the view that such pairs do not teach other cases, but what about the view that they do?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says 'they do not teach.' But for the one who says 'they do teach,' what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the previous answer from a new angle. The answer depended on one side of a known מחלוקת, so it may not work for the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 1 and 3 relied on the rule that 'two verses that come as one do not teach.' There is a known opinion that such verses DO teach other cases. According to that opinion, תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה together should teach a general rule, so the problem comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well (introduces a 'this is fine for one view, but...' challenge)
They do not teach (two verses with the same unusual law do not apply to other cases)
They do teach (the opposite opinion)
What is there to say? (the answer is missing)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is rejecting the answer it just gave. It does not take a side here. It only notes that there is a מחלוקת about whether two verses that come as one can teach other cases, and asks how the opposing view would explain the case.

phrases.english: It works out well for the one who says: they do not teach,
phrases.notes: This is the view that two פסוקים teaching the same rule can't be used to learn about other cases.

phrases.english: but for the one who says: they do teach,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין מְלַמְּדִין, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מְלַמְּדִין, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from Step 3 by pointing to the opposing view on 'two verses that come as one.'
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה are 'two verses that come as one' and therefore do not teach.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That answer only works for the view that such pairs do not teach. For the view that they do teach, the two cases should create a general rule.

steps.title: Each case has its own limiting word
steps.stepSummary: Both cases contain a limiting word in the פסוק: 'וְשָׂמוֹ' for תרומת הדשן and 'הָעֲרוּפָה' for עגלה ערופה. These words show that the law applies only to these cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two limiting words are written: 'and he shall put IT' and 'the one whose neck was broken.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Even the view that pairs of verses can teach would agree here, because the תורה itself limited each case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וְשָׂמוֹ' means he shall put IT, meaning only this ash and nothing else. 'הָעֲרוּפָה' points to THIS heifer alone. When the פסוק explicitly limits a law, no one learns a general rule from it, whatever their view on 'two verses that come as one.'

keyTerms.meaning: Limiting words (words in the פסוק that narrow a law to one case)
'And he shall put it' (ויקרא ו:ג), said of תרומת הדשן
'Whose neck was broken' (דברים כא:ו), said of עגלה ערופה

steps.whatToRemember: According to every opinion, תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה are exceptions that teach nothing about other cases. For the view that two verses do not teach, that rule alone is enough. For the view that they do teach, the limiting words 'וְשָׂמוֹ' and 'הָעֲרוּפָה' close the door.

phrases.english: Two limiting words are written:
"And he shall put it," and "whose neck was broken."
phrases.notes: The first refers to תרומת הדשן and the second to עגלה ערופה.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual limitation: each פסוק contains a word that restricts the law to its own case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For the view that pairs of verses teach, תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה would create a general rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The limiting words 'וְשָׂמוֹ' and 'הָעֲרוּפָה' block any general rule, even for that view.

steps.title: Why do we need three verses about blood?
steps.stepSummary: If nothing general can be learned from the exceptions, the default stands: once a מצוה is done, there is no מעילה. So why does the תורה need three verses to teach that leftover blood has no מעילה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And these three verses about blood, why do I need them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns back to the three phrases about blood mentioned earlier in the סוגיא. It asks why the תורה would need them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, three phrases in ויקרא יז:יא were used to teach that leftover blood, once its מצוה is done, has no מעילה. But we just learned that the exceptions teach nothing, so the normal rule is already 'after the מצוה, no מעילה.' So the verses look extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Three verses (here, three phrases in one פסוק)
Blood (here, the leftover blood of offerings after it has been placed on the מזבח)
Why do I need it? (asks why a source seems unnecessary)

phrases.english: And these three verses about blood —
phrases.notes: These are the phrases from ויקרא יז:יא that the גמרא quoted earlier.

phrases.english: why do I need them?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי תְּלָתָא קְרָאֵי בְּדָם לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from Step 5. Once the exceptions are limited, the verses about blood appear unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The three phrases about blood brought earlier in the סוגיא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the default rule already removes מעילה after the מצוה, the תורה would not need three verses to teach it for blood.

steps.title: Each verse removes blood from a different law
steps.stepSummary: Each of the three verses teaches something different. One removes blood from נותר, one from מעילה, and one from טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One verse excludes blood from נותר, one excludes it from מעילה, and one excludes it from טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the verses are not extra. Each one teaches a separate law about blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood of an offering is not treated like the offering's meat. Leftover blood does not bring the כרת of נותר. Eating it while טמא does not bring the punishment for eating קדשים בטומאה. And there is a verse for מעילה as well. The person is liable only for the ordinary איסור of eating blood.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude (to teach that a law does NOT apply)
Offering meat left past its time; eating it brings כרת
Misusing הקדש (consecrated property) for personal benefit
Ritual impurity (here, eating קדשים while impure)

phrases.english: One is to exclude it from notar,
and one is to exclude it from misuse of consecrated property,
and one is to exclude it from ritual impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 6 by giving each verse its own job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redistribution of verses: each verse teaches a separate exclusion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The three verses about blood seem extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verses exclude blood from נותר, מעילה, and טומאה, one law each.

steps.title: No verse is needed for פיגול
steps.stepSummary: There is no fourth verse for פיגול because none is needed. A משנה teaches that only things which have a מתיר are subject to פיגול. Blood is itself the מתיר, so פיגול never applies to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But to exclude blood from פיגול, no verse is needed. We learned in a משנה: anything that has something that permits it, whether for people or for the מזבח, one is liable for it because of פיגול. And blood is itself the thing that permits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes its answer by heading off an obvious question: why is there no verse excluding blood from פיגול? It brings a משנה to show that blood is already excluded by a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פיגול applies to parts of an offering that become permitted through something else, such as meat permitted by the sprinkling of blood. The blood is the thing doing the permitting, not something that gets permitted. So by the משנה's own rule, פיגול does not apply to blood, and no verse is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering made invalid by a wrong intention about time; eating it brings כרת
As we learned in a משנה (introduces a proof)
Things that make an offering permitted (such as the sprinkling of blood)
The altar

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the גמרא's careful reading of the תורה. Every verse must have a purpose, and the גמרא explains why each law about blood either needs a verse or is already covered by a general rule.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not misread 'כל שיש לו מתירין' as saying that the מתיר itself is subject to פיגול. It means the opposite: only things that are permitted BY a מתיר are subject to פיגול. The blood is the מתיר, so it is not included.
steps.whatToRemember: Blood of an offering is excluded from four laws: נותר, מעילה, and טומאה through three verses, and פיגול through the משנה's rule that the מתיר itself is not subject to פיגול.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מִפִּיגּוּל לָא צְרִיךְ לְמַעוֹטֵי קְרָא,
phrases.english: But to exclude it from piggul, no verse is needed,
as we learned in a mishna:
anything that has something that permits it,
whether for people or for the altar —
phrases.notes: The מתיר may allow people to eat the offering or allow it to go on the מזבח.

phrases.english: one is liable for it because of piggul.
And blood itself is the permitter.
phrases.notes: So blood is not something that gets permitted, and פיגול does not apply to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל מִפִּיגּוּל לָא צְרִיךְ לְמַעוֹטֵי קְרָא, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of Step 7 by explaining why there is no fourth verse for פיגול.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Anticipatory clarification backed by a משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might expect a fourth verse to exclude blood from פיגול.
steps.terutzMaskana: No verse is needed. By the משנה's rule, the מתיר itself is not subject to פיגול, and blood is the מתיר.
steps.raayaObject: That blood is not subject to פיגול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה 'כל שיש לו מתירין... חייבין עליו משום פיגול' (זבחים ד:ג).

steps.title: The יום הכיפורים service must follow its set order
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that every part of the יום הכיפורים service must be done in order. A step done too early does not count. If the goat's blood was sprinkled before the bull's, the goat's blood must be sprinkled again, after the bull's.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Every action of יום הכיפורים that is described is done in order. If he did one action before another, he has done nothing. If he sprinkled the goat's blood before the bull's blood, he must go back and sprinkle the goat's blood again after the bull's blood.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It states the basic rule that the order of the יום הכיפורים service is essential, and gives an example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that order is not just a nice extra: doing a step early makes that step not count. The example shows what this means in practice. The bull's blood was still done in its proper place, so it counts. Only the goat's blood, which came too early, has to be done again after it.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (here written in short as מַתְנִי׳)
In order; the steps must follow the set sequence
He did it earlier, ahead of its turn
He has done nothing; the act does not count
The blood of the goat / the blood of the bull

steps.confusionAlert: 'He has done nothing' does not mean the whole day is ruined. Only the step done out of order fails to count, and that step is redone in its correct place. The bull's blood, which was done properly, stays valid.

phrases.english: MISHNA
Every action of Yom Kippur that is stated
is done in order.
If he did one action before another,
he has done nothing.
If he put the goat's blood before the bull's blood,
he must go back and sprinkle from the goat's blood
after the bull's blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מַעֲשֵׂה יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הָאָמוּר — עַל הַסֵּדֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is not connected to the מעילה discussion that came before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The order of the יום הכיפורים service is essential. A step done out of order does not count and must be redone in its proper place.

steps.title: If the blood spills midway, restart that set of sprinklings
steps.stepSummary: If the blood spills before all the inside sprinklings are done, the כהן גדול brings new blood and restarts the inside sprinklings. The same applies in the היכל and on the מזבח הזהב. Each of these is its own separate atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the blood spilled before he finished the sprinklings inside, he brings other blood and starts again from the beginning of the inside sprinklings. The same is true in the Sanctuary and on the golden altar, because each one is a separate atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה deals with a new problem: the blood spills before a set of sprinklings is finished. It rules that the whole set is restarted with new blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The service has three separate sets of sprinklings: inside the קודש הקדשים, in the היכל, and on the מזבח הזהב. Each set counts as its own atonement. So a spill only means redoing the set that was interrupted, not the sets already finished. But within the interrupted set, he must start over from the beginning.

keyTerms.meaning: The sprinklings (literally 'gifts') of blood
The blood spilled
The Sanctuary, the room outside the קודש הקדשים
The golden altar, the incense altar in the היכל
Each is an atonement on its own

phrases.english: And if, before he finished
the sprinklings that are inside,
the blood spilled,
he must bring other blood
and start again from the beginning of the inside service.
And the same in the Sanctuary,
and the same on the golden altar,
since each of them is an atonement on its own.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא גָּמַר אֶת הַמַּתָּנוֹת שֶׁבִּפְנִים נִשְׁפַּךְ הַדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second case to the משנה: a set of sprinklings is interrupted by spilled blood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the blood spills partway through, he brings new blood and restarts only that set. Each set is its own separate atonement.

steps.title: A second view: continue from where you stopped
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון disagree with the previous view. They hold that after the blood spills, he continues with the new blood from the exact sprinkling where he stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say: from the place where he stopped, there he begins.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a dissenting opinion. They say there is no need to restart the set, only to continue from where he left off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא treats a whole set of sprinklings as one unit, so an interrupted set must be restarted. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון treat each single sprinkling as standing on its own. So the sprinklings already done stay valid, and he only adds the ones still missing.

keyTerms.meaning: He stopped or was interrupted
He begins (here: he resumes)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on spilled blood. The תנא קמא says restart the interrupted set. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say continue from the exact sprinkling where you stopped.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say:
From the place where he stopped,
there he begins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting view on the case in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the blood spills, he resumes with new blood from the exact sprinkling where he stopped.

steps.title: רבי יהודה limits the order rule to the inside service
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא repeats the משנה's rule that order is essential. רבי יהודה then limits it. It applies only to the service done in white garments inside. For white-garment service done outside, a step done out of order still counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The רבנן taught: every action of יום הכיפורים that is described is done in order, and if he did one before another, he has done nothing. רבי יהודה said: when is this so? For actions done in white garments inside. But for actions done in white garments outside, if he did one before another, what he did is done.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that repeats the משנה's rule. It then adds רבי יהודה's limit on which parts of the service the rule covers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'every action' sounds like it covers the whole day. רבי יהודה narrows it to the inside service, such as the קטורת and the blood sprinklings in the קודש הקדשים. For white-garment service done outside, such as the גורל and the וידוי, the order is only a starting instruction. If it was not followed, the step still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: The גמרא (here written in short as גְּמָ׳)
The Sages taught; introduces a ברייתא
When? (when does this rule apply)
The white linen garments of the כהן גדול on יום הכיפורים
Inside (the קודש הקדשים) / outside
What he did is done; it still counts

phrases.english: GEMARA
The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מַעֲשֵׂה יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הָאָמוּר — עַל הַסֵּדֶר.
phrases.english: Every action of Yom Kippur that is stated is done in order.
If he did one action before another,
he has done nothing.
Rabbi Yehuda said: When is this so?
For things done in white garments inside.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל דְּבָרִים הַנַּעֲשִׂין בְּבִגְדֵי לָבָן מִבַּחוּץ,
phrases.english: But for things done in white garments outside,
if he did one action before another,
what he did is done.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא turns to the scope of the משנה's rule from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: order is essential only for the white-garment service done inside. Outside white-garment service done out of order still counts.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה extends the rule to all white-garment service
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה holds that the order rule covers all white-garment service, inside or outside. Only the service done outside in golden garments still counts if done out of order.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה says: when is this said? For things done in white garments, whether inside or outside. But for things done in golden garments outside, what he did is done.
steps.whatsHappening: A second view in the ברייתא draws the line in a different place from רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי נחמיה, what matters is the type of garment, not where the service happens. All white-garment service is the special יום הכיפורים service, so its order is essential. Golden-garment service, such as the תמיד and the מוספין, is regular service, so the order there is not essential. The two views disagree only about white-garment service outside: רבי יהודה says it still counts, רבי נחמיה says it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case is this said? (introduces a limit on a rule)
The golden garments the כהן גדול wears for the regular service

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: order is essential only for inside white-garment service. רבי נחמיה: order is essential for all white-garment service, inside or out. Both agree that golden-garment service outside still counts if done out of order.

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya says:
In what case is this said?
For things done in white garments,
whether inside or outside.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בִּדְבָרִים הַנַּעֲשִׂים בְּבִגְדֵי זָהָב מִבַּחוּץ —
phrases.english: But for things done in golden garments outside,
what he did is done.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה אוֹמֵר: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing view to רבי יהודה's limit in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי נחמיה: order is essential for all white-garment service. Golden-garment service outside still counts if done out of order.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: both views come from the same verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה both learn their views from one פסוק: 'And this shall be an everlasting statute to you, once a year.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: both of them learned their view from one verse: 'And this shall be an everlasting statute to you … once a year.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן names the shared source for both views. This is a setup line: the גמרא will next explain how each one reads the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views agree that some of the service has an essential order. Their disagreement is only about which parts the פסוק covers. Quoting the פסוק sets up the explanation on the next amud, where each of them reads the פסוק differently.

keyTerms.meaning: They learned their views from one verse
A statute; a word often read to mean the detail is essential
Once a year; points to the service that is unique to יום הכיפורים

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
And both of them learned their view from one verse:
"And this shall be for you
an everlasting statute
once a year,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source behind the two views in steps 12 and 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה learn their views from the פסוק 'an everlasting statute … once a year'. Each reads it differently, as the גמרא explains on the next amud.
